description: M6/M7 vs. the alternative (docs/vision/27-strengths-bench.md §6, plan docs/plans/strengths-bench.md SB-32): the home lookup corpus (testdata/contextbench/tasks-home.json, ids kept, prompts and ground truth copied verbatim) run as scenariobench tasks with five arms — full (fathom, wired), graphify, serena, gopls (each a competitor's own MCP tool documented in docs/bench/competitors.md), and grep (no MCP at all). Every arm gets Read/Grep/Bash; only 'full' is wired and gets the fathom stanza ('stanza'); every other arm's instructions variant is 'plain' — the subject's own files, untouched. This corpus's tasks are LOOKUPS, not code changes, so Oracle (fail_to_pass/pass_to_pass/coverage) is deliberately left empty for every task: the graded answer is a short string, not a test result. The expected ground truth for each task lives in notes.gold (SB-32's instruction: 'put gold under notes'), keyed by task id, copied from tasks-home.json's own ground_truth/scoring_rule/class fields — see notes.gold_source for the exact pointer instead of duplicating tasks-home.json's multi-paragraph provenance essays here. A FRESHNESS task (id FRESH-M7-01, category 'freshness', M7) is added: its Subject.Setup writes a brand-new file and function AFTER the arm's own setup has already run — see notes.freshness_run_order for the ordering assumption this task depends on, flagged for whoever implements PrepareSubject/RenderArm (plan wave 2, SB-11/SB-12, not built yet). Task categories for the 13 lookup tasks are hand-assigned from tasks-home.json's own class taxonomy (obligations, verify, blast_radius, claim_provenance, concern_search, contradiction, staleness) per types.go's 'Category ... assigned by ... hand with a derivation note' allowance — none of them are a ClassifyChange shape, because none of them is a code change.

full.prediction: Wins the obligations/verify/staleness lookups outright (no competitor tool answers governance questions at all); wins or ties the two structural lookups (2-hop callers, interface implementers) via find_callers/blast_radius and find_symbol's implementations field; wins the freshness task because the wired worktree is (re-)ingested after the scripted edit lands; ties everyone on the pure-prose contradiction task, where no index has an edge.

graphify.prediction: Its query_graph/get_neighbors/shortest_path tools answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (a direct calls-relation edge, its home turf); a predicted loss on the interface-implementers lookup (no type-checker, so implicit Go interface satisfaction is outside what tree-sitter extraction can encode); a predicted loss on the freshness task (its graph.json is a precomputed artifact built during this arm's own setup, before the freshness edit lands, and this arm's setup runs no --update afterward).
graphify.notes: setup is the headless CLI build (graphify update <path> --no-cluster: tree-sitter only, no LLM, no plugin install) — `graphify install` writes a Claude Code skill into the user's global config and `/graphify .` is an in-session slash command, neither of which a bench may run (docs/bench/competitors.md)

serena.prediction: find_symbol/find_referencing_symbols/find_implementations answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (find_referencing_symbols chained twice) and the interface-implementers lookup (find_implementations is backed by gopls's real type-checker — single-language references and implementations are its home turf, docs/vision/27-strengths-bench.md §6); a predicted tie with fathom on the freshness task, since its gopls backend re-analyzes the file on disk on every call — no precomputed artifact to go stale.

gopls.prediction: go_symbol_references/go_references answer code structure, not documented governance rules, so it is predicted to tie the grep arm (not fathom) on every obligations/verify/staleness lookup; a plausible tie with fathom on the 2-hop caller lookup (go_symbol_references chained twice) — single-language references is its home turf; a predicted tie with fathom on the freshness task, since it re-analyzes the file on disk on every call — no precomputed artifact to go stale. No find_implementations-equivalent is in its tool list here, so the interface-implementers lookup is predicted weaker than serena's, closer to a textual match.

grep.prediction: Predicted below fathom on the obligations/verify/staleness lookups (the fact is on disk and grep-findable given the right file, but nothing points it at that file the way fathom's own tool does) and on the 2-hop caller lookup (nothing prompts a second grep once the first plausible-looking direct caller is found — the home-bench's own empirical run found fathom beats grep on exactly this task shape); predicted tied with fathom on the pure-prose contradiction task; predicted tied with fathom on the freshness task, since a direct file read always reflects the file's current on-disk content.

notes.freshness_run_order: FRESH-M7-01 depends on a run-order guarantee that is not yet enforced by any built code (PrepareSubject/RenderArm are plan wave 2, SB-11/SB-12, not implemented as of this corpus's authoring): each arm's OWN setup — graphify's '/graphify .' build, or the wired arm's fathom-init worktree ingest — must run BEFORE this task's Subject.Setup writes internal/store/freshnessmarker.go. If Subject.Setup instead ran first, every arm (including graphify) would see the new file at build/ingest time and the freshness comparison would measure nothing. Flagged here for the wave-2 implementer rather than silently assumed.
